title: Progression Day Count in Work Conditioning and Work Hardening
content:
# Progression day count

**Definition.** In the hour-billed programs of the Workers' Compensation Referral — Work Conditioning Program and Work Hardening Program — the progression day count of a program day is:

- the calendar days from the suspension start date on file, where the referral's latest suspension began no more than twenty-one (21) calendar days before the day of service;
- the calendar days since the initial evaluation less seven (7), where that suspension began twenty-two to forty-two (22 to 42) calendar days before the day of service; and
- the calendar days since the initial evaluation otherwise — including a referral with no suspension start date on file, and a suspension that began more than 42 calendar days before.

The initial evaluation is the date of service of the referral's evaluation charge. The latest suspension is the one whose start date is on the referral record.

## Bands at a glance

| Latest suspension began, before the day of service | Progression day count |
|---|---|
| 0 to 21 calendar days | calendar days from the suspension start date |
| 22 to 42 calendar days | calendar days since the initial evaluation, less 7 |
| more than 42 days, or no suspension on file | calendar days since the initial evaluation |

## Edges of the bands

- A suspension that began exactly 21 days before falls in the first band; one that began 22 days before falls in the second.
- A suspension that began exactly 42 days before falls in the second band; one that began 43 days before falls in the third.

## Worked cases (hypothetical dates, counted in calendar days before the day of service)

| Initial evaluation | Latest suspension began | Band | Progression day count |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30 days before | 10 days before | first | 10 |
| 40 days before | 25 days before | second | 40 less 7, that is 33 |
| 40 days before | 50 days before | third | 40 |
| 18 days before | none on file | third | 18 |
